Yes, for any commit that gets replayed. A commit's hash covers its tree, parent hash(es), author, committer, timestamp, and message. Rebase gives each replayed commit a new parent, which changes the hash, and that cascades to every descendant.

Commits that stay unchanged at the start of the rebased range (a fast-forwarded prefix, or commits below the new base) keep their hashes. If the rebase is a no-op, nothing changes. This is why rebasing already-pushed commits requires a force push and can disrupt others who based work on the old hashes.
